REQ-1.title: A job is given the approved design and requirement it builds

REQ-2.title: Issue status says who the issue waits on

REQ-3.title: Agent narration is separated from human conversation

REQ-4.title: Business intent has a versioned home

REQ-5.title: A project can agree an interface with itself before building both sides

REQ-6.title: Verdicts are typed records, not comment prose

REQ-7.title: Product feedback is a first-class item, triaged and verified by people

REQ-8.title: Assistant proposals wait for a person

REQ-9.title: Cross-project work waits on a contract version

REQ-10.title: A new project gets its key journeys drawn with the user before building

REQ-11.title: Development: a person sees what is running, what is stuck and what waits on them, per issue, module, contract and release

REQ-12.title: Every Forge screen and entity is built to one set of conventions

REQ-13.title: What an agent writes for a project follows that project's rules, not Forge's

REQ-14.title: The Development area and Releases are built to the prototype

REQ-15.title: Agents / Runs: a person reads every run's standing, its holder and what the project master is doing, from one core read model

REQ-16.title: Automation: one area shows what fires, what each fire produced, and what needs a person

REQ-17.title: A workflow design shows which steps and lines are outdated, need an update, have a problem or are proposed for removal, each derived from its evidence

REQ-18.title: Design is the root; code is reconciled to it, by observation, marking, decision and rewrite

REQ-19.title: Chat has two modes: assistant mode answers from a model with the key set in the instance environment, and agent mode runs on the team's runner

REQ-20.title: A question an agent parks reaches the people who owe the answer in the team's chat channel, and their reply there answers it

REQ-21.title: A project connects its storefront — Autoflow by OAuth, or ePodSystem — and its agents read shop, theme and draft data and publish drafts through Forge without ever holding the credential

REQ-22.title: An operator reads Forge's own service health — alert levels, pipeline health and the MCP audit trail — on one console, and is notified when an alert crosses into warn or crit

REQ-23.title: A person or an agent reads how each Forge capability is used from one guide corpus Forge serves publicly, and the prompts Forge composes point at the guide instead of restating it

REQ-24.title: A member reads each project's health and its trend — throughput, step failures, retries and interventions — on the project dashboard, derived from records Forge already keeps

REQ-25.title: A person installs the runner on a box with one command Forge serves, which fetches the published build for that box's platform

REQ-26.title: A project pins the plugin version its runs use, and a box serving several projects reports a conflicting pin instead of silently picking one

REQ-27.title: People sign in with a password or Google and agents act with personal access tokens, and invitations and notices reach people by mail

REQ-28.title: Every design template carries structured cross-design refs, checked to resolve to an approved revision step

REQ-29.title: Requirements carry an area the list groups and filters by

REQ-30.title: Assistant and Agent chat: role, routing and limits

REQ-31.title: The Ask Agent panel opens at its largest width, toggles to half of it, and the page beside it stays usable at either size

REQ-32.title: Chat answers visually: reports, diagrams, templates, share links

REQ-33.title: Decisions, roadmap and memory are read inside the item they are about, not on pages of their own

REQ-34.title: Every lifecycle step is a checklist contract that people and agents must complete, and the kernel enforces it

REQ-35.title: Every Product item reads as a picture first

REQ-36.title: Delivery: each role designs and tests only its own scope

REQ-37.title: Scripts read Forge with GET only, under a short-lived token of their owner

REQ-38.title: QA probe 209: a person can see the build version in the footer

REQ-39.title: See a change live before it ships

REQ-40.title: Every release is a readable page, led by the Product

REQ-41.title: Chat is the way in: it answers what needs you and drives the page beside it

automation.title: Automation: fires, what they produced, triage

core-components.title: Core components: doors, domains and adapters around the kernel

design-reconciliation.title: Design reconciliation: code reconciled to the approved design

github-merge-sequence.title: Change request merged to merge evidence

workflow-step-health.title: Workflow step health: provenance and markers derived from evidence
